Subject: Access problem: supplier portal token mismatch & PO visibility

Hi Sergio,

We tried to accept the supplier portal invite you sent this morning and ran into a blocking issue. Clicking the invite link takes us to the portal login, we sign in via our Okta SSO, then the page redirects back to the invite handler and immediately drops to an error page that says: "Token mismatch — claim invalid or expired."

We tried three different people here (me, gethyn, and our AP mailbox) and the behavior is identical. The portal account is created, but after login none of our recent POs are visible in the dashboard (they show 0 POs). We need to acknowledge PO #HH-4821 by tomorrow morning.

Attached a quick screenshot of the error (sso-error-20270629.png) and our support team can share logs if helpful.

Environment details:
- Company SSO: hartley.okta.com (SAML)
- Users tested on Windows 10 with Chrome 113 and on Mac Safari 15
- We are behind a corporate proxy that performs URL rewriting for tracking: sometimes it appends "utm_src=corpproxy" to query strings

Can you advise? If this needs an engineering fix we can open a change window — urgent for PO acknowledgement.

Thanks,
Olivia Hartley
Procurement Manager
Hartley Hardware

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Access problem: supplier portal token mismatch & PO visibility

Hi Olivia — thanks for the report and the screenshot. Sorry you're seeing this. Two quick asks so we can triage fast: 

1) Can you forward a small portion of the browser network log around the redirect (capture the request to "/auth/claim?token=..."). A pasted request line + query string is enough.
2) Can you confirm whether the invite link you clicked contains additional extra parameters after the token (any "utm_" query params, tracking GUIDs, or proxy-added fragments)?

Initial hypothesis: our invite claim endpoint validates the token signature and also checks that the redirect URL exactly matches the token-bound URL. If your proxy is rewriting the invite URL (appending query params or changing encoding), the token validation can fail with a "token mismatch" error. We had a similar-looking case where corporate proxies appended tracking tags and broke the claim signature.

Workarounds to try immediately (non-destructive):
- Open an incognito/private window and paste the raw invite link into the address bar (do not click from the email client).
- If the link was forwarded, ask the original recipient to request a re-send from our portal (we can force a fresh token).

I'll loop in Ben and Kim to check if we can reissue an invite with an alternate accept flow (force-new-token / claim-tolerant redirect) while we verify proxy behavior. If you can paste the claim request line here that will speed things up.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

I can confirm the invite link we received from your system had the token only, but after our proxy the browser shows the appended "utm_src=corpproxy" parameter. When I paste the original invite URL directly into the address bar (raw token, no utm param) the claim proceeds much further — it creates our portal account and shows a brief loading state — but eventually the PO list still reads 0 (we expected to see HH-4821). So there might be two separate issues: 1) the proxy parameter causing token mismatch for some users, and 2) missing PO mapping for accounts created through this flow.

I attached a short server-side excerpt from our IT team (claim-log.txt) — it shows the redirect sequence and the proxy rewrite.

Let us know the best next steps. If reissuing an invite with a tolerance flag will definitely fix at least the token error we'll do that for the PO-critical users.

Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the log snippets, that was very helpful. Summary of findings & action items: 

Findings:
- The token mismatch is reproducible when an extra query parameter is appended to the invite URL (your proxy adds "utm_src=corpproxy"). Our claim verifier expects the token-bound URL to match; extra params break the signature check.
- The missing PO visibility appears to be a separate mapping issue: accounts created via the invite claim route occasionally skip an attribute we use to surface POs (we've reproduced in staging).

Immediate remediation (what we'll do now):
1) Ben will reissue a short-lived invite for the three users you mentioned, using the "force-new-token" flag which makes our claim endpoint ignore non-token query params for the first accept attempt. This requires no code change and is safe; token will expire in 4 hours.
2) Kim will file a low-risk patch to relax redirect-encoding matching so trackers like "utm_src" are ignored for token validation (SUP-8241). We will push this to a staging rollout today and coordinate a small production deploy tomorrow evening if green.
3) I recommend your IT whitelist portal.redwood-inference.com in the proxy tracking rules as a long-term fix; Kim attached a short whitelisting guide (support-kb-proxy-whitelist.md).

Workaround for you now: open the raw invite link in an incognito/private window and paste the URL (do not click), or wait for the reissued invites (Ben will send). If the POs are still missing after claim success please reply and we will map HH-4821 manually for the short term.

Ben / Kim — can you confirm when the new invites are sent and paste the invite IDs here so Olivia can try immediately?

Olivia — I'll follow up once SUP-8241 is in staging. Apologies for the friction and thanks for the quick diagnostics — that log made the cause clear.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
